$comment: Full quality pipeline: design → implement → internal review → gate → PR → CI/external-review loop → human-approved merge. Recommendation encoded here (not enforced by the engine): give reviewer_external a DIFFERENT model than fixer/implementer — a second pair of eyes from another model family finds different bugs. Map roles to your project's agents in your own config.

pipeline.prompt:
Design pre-flight for: {{feature.title}}.
Produce a short design note (decisions, trade-offs, file plan). Then call conductor_report with outcome=succeeded and the FULL design note as the output — later steps run in fresh sessions and only see what you report.

Implement: {{feature.title}}.
Design note:
{{steps.design.output}}

Work in {{feature.worktree}} on branch {{feature.branch}}. Commit as you go.
When the implementation is complete, call conductor_report with outcome=succeeded and notes shaped as a PR description in markdown — they become the pull request body verbatim:
## Summary\n<what and why, 2-4 sentences>\n## Changes\n<bulleted list: file/area — what changed>\n## Test plan\n<how it is verified: tests added/run, commands>
Write it for a human reviewer seeing the PR cold.

Pre-push review of the work in {{feature.worktree}} (diff against {{config.baseBranch}}).
Review for correctness, tests, and project conventions.
Report your findings STRUCTURED: pass notes as a JSON object {"summary": "<overall assessment, markdown>", "findings": [{"path": "src/file.ts", "line": 42, "side": "RIGHT", "severity": "blocker|major|minor|nit", "tags": ["correctness"], "body": "<what is wrong + what you expect>"}]} — this is a pre-push review: nothing is published, the findings go straight to the fixer.
Severity scale: blocker = broken behaviour/data loss/security hole; major = a bug or a missing test for an error path; minor = real quality improvement; nit = taste. Omitted severity counts as major. tags are free-form labels (correctness, tests, style, security, scope...).
Verdict follows findings: any blocker or major ⇒ changes_requested; only minor/nit ⇒ approved (they still get published as comments).
Then call conductor_report with verdict=approved or verdict=changes_requested and those notes.

Internal review requested changes.
Open findings (source of truth, from the conductor database):
{{findings.open}}

Severity contract: blocker/major MUST be fixed; minor — fix or justify; nit — may dismiss with one sentence.
Apply fixes in {{feature.worktree}}, commit.
For EVERY finding listed above report a resolution: call conductor_report with outcome=succeeded and notes as JSON:
{"resolutions": [{"id": "F1", "status": "fixed", "note": "<what you changed>"}, {"id": "F2", "status": "dismissed", "note": "<why no change is needed>"}], "summary": "<one paragraph>"}

CI for PR #{{feature.pr}} is red on SHA {{feature.head_sha}}.
Failed checks:
{{steps.await_ci.output}}

Work in {{feature.worktree}}. Diagnose, apply the smallest fix, commit and push. Then call conductor_report with outcome=succeeded (or failed with a reason).

Review PR #{{feature.pr}} (repo {{config.repo}}) at SHA {{feature.head_sha}}.
Read the diff with gh, inspect the code in {{feature.worktree}} (read-only).

Previously recorded findings (do not re-raise fixed/dismissed ones):
{{findings.digest}}

On repeat rounds judge ONLY the new commits since your previous review. Do NOT raise new minor/nit findings on code you already approved — approved means approved. If a fixed/dismissed finding is genuinely NOT addressed, say so in the summary and report it again with body prefixed '[reopen F<n>]'.

Report your findings STRUCTURED: pass notes as a JSON object {"summary": "<overall assessment, markdown>", "findings": [{"path": "src/file.ts", "line": 42, "side": "RIGHT", "severity": "blocker|major|minor|nit", "tags": ["correctness"], "body": "<what is wrong + what you expect>"}]} — the conductor records each finding in its database (the source of truth), publishes the review to the PR under the configured identity, and routes the findings to the fixer. Do NOT post to GitHub yourself.
Severity: blocker = broken behaviour/data loss/security; major = bug or missing error-path test; minor = real improvement; nit = taste. Omitted severity counts as major.
Verdict follows findings: any blocker or major => changes_requested; only minor/nit => approved.
Then call conductor_report with verdict=approved or verdict=changes_requested and those notes.
